correctness.rationale: The finite arc complex is fully enumerated (16,80,144,72 simplices) and dimension at most three by the two-left-vertex degree bound. CHECK.py constructs and proves acyclicity of 147 matched pairs, verifies every integral unit-pivot chain cancellation, computes reduced signed differentials with Smith factors (1) and (1,1,1,2) and checks the chain identity. Consequently integral H2 is Z^7 plus Z/2, not merely finite-field homology. Independent FIELD_CHECK.py reproduces full boundary ranks in five characteristics, with the UCT-predicted characteristic-two increment. The original Definitions 4.1–4.4 require edgeful connected full regions and stable boundary vertices; every arc of bidirected K(2,4) lies in a directed 2-cycle and any proper edgeful region has an unstable boundary, so the entire graph is the unique unstable module. Limits: finite exhaustiveness does not imply a family theorem or minimality.

originality.rationale: The exact target article arXiv:2208.04656v1 makes torsion-implies-stability a conjecture. Its Section 4 covers other oriented graph families. The strongest relevant later paper, arXiv:2401.01248v1, bounds torsion in fixed genus and compares directed and matching complexes only absent directed cycles; neither implies an integral order-two class in bidirected K(2,4). Actual semantic searches and primary-material inspections found only distinct complexes, graphs or coefficient fields. This is best-knowledge originality, with unindexed literature risk.

value.rationale: The exact second-integral-homology 2-torsion of a canonical six-vertex bidirected complete-bipartite graph directly falsifies a published structural conjecture about torsion and dynamical-module stability. The unique-module argument is decisive and avoids arbitrary numerical slicing. The result motivates revised torsion conditions without claiming a classification or minimal counterexample.
